title: Vienna Rising Again
premise: Hazel Thornbury, a private security contractor with a fabricated past, is guarding a nervous data-broker in Vienna when the broker's inbound flight vanishes from every record while still airborne. The trail leads to Meridian, the deniable training network that once made Hazel who they are — and that holds the only proof of what really happened aboard that plane. As Hazel burns through Meridian's cells of handlers and safehouses, they must choose between loyalty to the mentor who saved them and the truth that could free them, culminating in a dawn confrontation at a border checkpoint where Hazel trades their polished lie for the raw record, letting Meridian fall even as it costs them everything they built to hide.
about_author: X. M. Ishikawa is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent years shuttling between Central European capitals before turning to fiction full-time. They write thrillers about people whose paperwork matters more than their names.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A routine protection detail in Vienna: coffee, sightlines, a client who flinches at his own phone. We learn Hazel keeps a go-bag packed and a biography that doesn't survive scrutiny. Emotional beat: controlled unease — the calm of someone always halfway gone.

chapters.title: Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The client, data-broker Anton Reisz, hires Hazel for one week and pays in cash, hinting he's carrying something 'that flies.' Hazel runs background checks that come back too clean. Emotional beat: professional suspicion hardening into instinct — everyone lies; Hazel just wants to know which lie this is.

chapters.title: Flight 4471
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Reisz insists on meeting an associate arriving on Flight 4471 from Zurich. At the gate, the departures board blinks: flight canceled. But radar apps show it still airborne. Ground staff have no record it ever existed. Emotional beat: vertigo — the world's records just disagreed with reality.

chapters.title: Erased Mid-Air
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with a brief intercut of air-traffic controller Nadia Brandt. The plane lands anyway, unlisted, at a military-adjacent strip. The associate never appears; Reisz panics and bolts. Hazel chooses to follow rather than report. Emotional beat: the first deliberate step off the legal map.

chapters.title: What Meridian Made
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Following Reisz's dead-drops, Hazel recognizes tradecraft — dead-letter boxes, brush passes — from their own training years ago under a program called Meridian. Someone from the old network is running Vienna. Emotional beat: dread curdling into recognition; the past isn't behind them, it's operational.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Voice
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A call from Ilsa Voss, Hazel's former handler, offering extraction and warning Hazel off. Her voice still carries the authority of the person who rebuilt Hazel after the war. Emotional beat: loyalty pulling like gravity against the growing suspicion that Voss is inside whatever happened to Flight 4471.

chapters.title: Reisz in the Canal District
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel finds Reisz hiding in a canal-side safe flat, clutching an encrypted drive: passenger manifests and cargo logs proving Flight 4471 carried people, not freight — and that Meridian sold them onward. Emotional beat: reluctant guardianship; Hazel now protects the truth whether they want to or not.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Protocol
chapters.summary: Nadia Brandt's POV. The controller, quietly investigating the phantom flight, notices Hazel asking the same questions she is. She shares radar archives; Hazel shares nothing true about themselves. Emotional beat: two liars circling a fragile, transactional trust.

chapters.title: Burn Notice, Old Style
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Meridian cleaners hit Reisz's flat minutes after they leave. Hazel realizes the network has flagged them — the student has become a target. They move Reisz using techniques Voss taught them, hating how well the lessons hold. Emotional beat: grief for the self the training built.

chapters.title: The Lie Polished
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, flashback-woven. Under pressure from a Meridian interrogator posing as a police liaison, Hazel deploys the false biography they've rehearsed for a decade — and watches it work perfectly. Emotional beat: hollow triumph; the lie saves them and reminds them how much of them is counterfeit.

chapters.title: Nadia's Ledger
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia reconstructs the flight path and finds the aircraft's transponder was spoofed by ground equipment owned through seven shells — all touching Meridian front companies. She gives Hazel the ledger copy. Emotional beat: quiet courage; a civilian choosing the dangerous side of the record.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Holed up with Reisz, Hazel counts exits, hours, and betrayals. Reisz confesses he wasn't a whistleblower — he was the broker who arranged the flight's cargo. Emotional beat: fury and calculation colliding; justice outside the law starts looking like leverage, not virtue.

chapters.title: Voss at the Prater
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Voss surfaces in person beneath the Riesenrad, offering Hazel reinstatement, protection, and Reisz's clean disappearance — if Hazel hands over the drive. She claims the flight was sanctioned above her. Emotional beat: the loyalty-vs-truth fault line cracking open; Hazel wants to believe her more than they should.

chapters.title: Half a Truth
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel tests Voss's story against Nadia's ledger and finds it half-true: the operation was sanctioned, but Voss ran it off-book and sold the passengers' route to a third party. The mentor is both victim and architect. Emotional beat: betrayal refined into clarity.

chapters.title: The Cell in Hietzing
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel raids a Meridian safehouse cell, recovering the network's Vienna roster and the schedule of border checkpoint shift changes — the narrow window when the corrupted system goes blind. Emotional beat: cold momentum; the plan assembles itself out of stolen paper.

chapters.title: Reisz Runs
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Terrified, Reisz tries to sell the drive to a journalist and walks into a Meridian ambush. Hazel extracts him wounded, losing the decoy drive in the process. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening resolve — Hazel can't save everyone, but they can finish this.

chapters.title: Nadia in the Crosshairs
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Meridian traces the ledger leak to Nadia; she survives a staged accident and goes dark, delivering herself to Hazel. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into partnership — the controller and the contractor, both now unrecorded people.

chapters.title: The Window Opens
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. With the checkpoint shift change ninety minutes away, Hazel splits the plan: Nadia will push the full flight record to three jurisdictions simultaneously; Hazel will physically deliver the original drive through the checkpoint where Meridian's blind spot lives. Emotional beat: taut readiness — no more running, only timing.

chapters.title: Voss's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Voss intercepts Hazel en route, and in a brutal, intimate fight Hazel finally refuses the lesson — defeating her with improvisation instead of Meridian doctrine. Wounded, Voss tells Hazel the truth she withheld: the passengers were witnesses to a Meridian atrocity. Emotional beat: sorrowful severance; loyalty dies so truth can breathe.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the border checkpoint, in the minutes when the old shift stands down and the new one signs in, Hazel walks the drive through, uploading the record as Meridian's last cleaners close in. Sirens, jurisdictional pings, the network's own channels flooding with exposure. Emotional beat: white-knuckle climax; the truth crosses the line a heartbeat ahead of the bullets.

chapters.title: Records Restored
chapters.summary: Alternating Hazel/Nadia POV. Flight 4471 reappears in official databases; arrests ripple through shell companies; Nadia testifies under protection. Hazel, officially a ghost, watches the news from a tram window beside a newly packed go-bag they don't pick up. Emotional beat: exhausted release — justice arrived sideways, but it arrived.

chapters.title: Vienna Rising Again
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Weeks later, Hazel burns the false biography for good, mails Reisz's testimony to the journalist, and stays in Vienna — unpacked, unpolished, unnamed in every file that matters. A letter arrives from an unknown number: 'We trained you better than this.' Hazel smiles and lets it burn. Emotional beat: quiet rebirth; the person left when the lie is gone.
